$note: Synthetic, labeled demo applications. Each captures the evidence story of a realistic Ethiopian SME applicant. Uses the canonical application shape.

applications.label: Alpha Foods Enterprise
applications.scenario: Strong food-processing MSE: women-owned, growing sales, local sourcing. User sent data via text.
shots: Our company is Alpha Foods Enterprise, a food processing company.
We have been operating since 2019 and we are 100% women-owned.
Last year (2024) our sales were 12 million birr; in 2023 they were 8 million.
We have 25 employees; 12 of them are women and 10 are youth between 18 and 24.
We buy 90% of our raw materials locally.
We plan to create 35 new jobs.
We also reduce waste by recycling by-products into animal feed, which helps the environment and creates community jobs.

applications.label: Beta Textiles PLC
applications.scenario: Medium textile company. Employment over 10 → C7b routing. Mixed market (local + export).
shots: Our name is Beta Textiles PLC, we manufacture garments and fabrics.
We started in 2019 and are owned 60% by women.
In 2023 we had 130 employees; in 2024 we employ 145 people, 80 of them women.
2023 sales were 19 million birr, and in 2024 sales reached 26 million.
Our registration number is REG-BTX-2019-442.
We sell mostly locally but we export some to the region.
We differentiate ourselves with in-house design and we use imported equipment.
We expect to add 60 jobs next year.
Our production also supports decent work: we provide safety and health training to all staff.
We have 40 workers aged between 18 and 24.
We purchase 70% of our cotton and fabric locally.
Expected results: expand export capacity, train 30 new seamstresses, and reduce fabric waste by 20%.
Core management team: Sara Tesfaye as General Manager, Hanna Bekele as Finance Lead, and Dawit Girma as Production Manager.
Our investment readiness score is 26 out of 30.

applications.label: GreenTech Energy Solutions
applications.scenario: Solar distribution company with strong SDG1/7/13 overlap. High local sourcing.
shots: We are GreenTech Energy Solutions; we distribute and install solar panels.
Founded in 2018, owned 100% by two male founders.
2023 revenue was 5.5 million birr; 2024 revenue was 9 million birr.
We have 18 employees, 4 women; 6 are youth aged under 25.
About 85% of components come from local suppliers.
We will create 12 new jobs when the warehouse expands.
Our products replace diesel generators, cutting emissions and giving rural households reliable power.

applications.label: Roza Handicrafts Cooperative
applications.scenario: Women's handicraft cooperative, local market, moderate sales.
shots: ስማችን ሮዛ ሃንድክራፍት ኮኦፕሬቲቭ ነው። በእጅ የተሰሩ ጌጣጌጦች እንሰራለን።
ከ2016 ጀምረን እየሰራን ነው። 100% በሴቶች የተያዘ ነው።
2023 ሽያጭ 2 ሚሊዮን ነበር፣ 2024 ሽያጭ 2.8 ሚሊዮን ነበር።
9 ሰራተኞች አሉን፣ ሁሉም ሴቶች ናቸው።
ጥሬ ዕቃዎቻችንን በሙሉ ከአካባቢው ገበያ እንገዛለን።

ሴቶችን በማብቃት እና ባህላዊ ቅርሶችን በማስተዋወቅ ላይ እንሰራለን።

applications.label: Dagim Import & Trade
applications.scenario: Import/trading company. Older. Mixed ownership. Higher turnover, lower impact.
shots: Our company is Dagim Import and Trade, we import spare parts and sell wholesale.
We have been operating for 12 years, since 2014.
Ownership is 50% women and 50% men.
Sales: 2023 = 45 million, 2024 = 52 million birr.
In 2023 we had 35 employees; in 2024 we employ 40 people; 8 are women, 5 are youth.
Our registration number is TD/DG-2014-0931.
We import 100% of our products (no local sourcing).
We do not plan to create additional jobs this year.
We support the local economy by providing parts that keep vehicles running.
Expected results: serve 3 new regions, stock more spare-part lines, and improve warehouse turnaround by 15%.
Core management team: Dagim Tadesse as Managing Director, Meron Haile as Operations Manager, and Chala Bekele as Warehouse Supervisor.
We differentiate ourselves with a nationwide spare-parts distribution network no competitor has.
Our investment readiness score is 22 out of 30.

applications.label: SolarFix Repair Services
applications.scenario: Small repair service. Missing data: no ownership, no job creation numbers. Gaps visible.
shots: Hello, we are SolarFix, we repair solar panels and inverters in Addis Ababa.
We started working in 2021.
In 2024 our revenue was 1.5 million birr.
We have 6 employees.
We serve households and small businesses in our neighborhood.
We want to grow and serve more customers.

applications.label: Kebede Family Farm PLC
applications.scenario: Agriculture/poultry. Contradiction present: sales 2024 stated as 3 million then 9 million.
shots: Kebede Family Farm PLC is a poultry farm outside Addis.
Started in 2011; family-owned.
In 2024 our sales were 3 million birr.
Wait — I mean 9 million birr in 2024 sales.
We have 30 employees, 10 of them women.
We source 70% of feed locally.
We want to create 15 new jobs.

applications.label: Selam Logistics Services
applications.scenario: Service company with strong recent growth and job ambitions.
shots: Selam Logistics runs a small fleet of trucks in Addis.
Founded in 2020.
2023 sales: 4 million; 2024 sales: 6.5 million.
In 2023 we had 17 employees; in 2024 we have 22 employees and 3 women drivers.
7 of our staff are aged 18-24.
Our registration number is REG-SLM-2020-112.
The company is owned 60% by women and 40% by men.
We buy 90% of our fuel and maintenance locally.
We plan to create 20 jobs and expand our fleet with the loan.
Better logistics reduces road congestion and supports local factories.
Expected results: add 5 delivery routes, reduce vehicle idle time 20%, and open one regional depot.
Core management team: Selam Bekele as General Manager, Tesfaye Alemu as Fleet Manager, and Hanna Girma as Depot Manager.
We are the only logistics firm offering overnight cold-chain delivery in Addis.
Our investment readiness score is 24 out of 30.

applications.label: Tekle Metal Works
applications.scenario: Metal fabrication, manufacturing, few details on uniqueness.
shots: Tekle Metal Works produces metal doors and window frames.
We began in 2017; one owner.
2024 sales: 7 million birr.
We have 15 employees, 2 women.
Our products are essential for construction in Addis.
We plan to hire 10 more workers.

applications.label: Abay Ceramics Manufacturing
shots: Abay Ceramics makes tiles and sanitary ware.
We have operated for 8 years (since 2018).
Owners are two brothers (men). The company is owned 0% by women and 100% by men.
Our registration number is REG-ABY-2018-077.
2023 sales: 14 million; 2024 sales: 18 million birr.
In 2023 we had 130 employees; in 2024 we have 150 employees, 22 women, 60 youth.
Our tiles replaced imports from abroad — we are one of three producers in Ethiopia.
We plan to create 40 jobs and build a new kiln.
We use local clay and recycle production water; we source 85% of our raw materials locally.
We are the first Ethiopian producer to make sanitary ware with local clay — it is new to Ethiopia.
Expected results: build a new kiln, raise annual output by 30%, and certify quality standards.
Core management team: Abay Wondimu as General Manager, Lemlem Assefa as Finance Head, and Girma Belete as Plant Manager.
Our investment readiness score is 28 out of 30.

applications.label: Meron Leather Accessories

shots: Meron Leather makes bags and belts from Ethiopian leather.
Started in 2022; 100% women-owned.
2023 sales 0.9M, 2024 sales 1.4M birr.
5 employees, all women.
We buy 95% of our leather locally.
We plan to create 10 new jobs; actually we expect to create 25 new jobs this year.
